title: Copilot Studio: self-learning recommendations to refine agents
summary: Hold: testing is presented as an unavoidable consumption cost, but Microsoft documents unbilled test-chat activity and agent-flow test runs, and the feature's harness is unknown. The roadmap facts and cited monthly-limit path are supported; the controls guidance also needs qualifications and missing control rows.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Credits are the documented unit for Copilot Studio agent usage.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure agent usage. One interaction with an agent can consume several credits because each feature the agent uses in that interaction has its own rate.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agent flows are predefined flow-action sequences that avoid reasoning and orchestration at each step.
claims.quote: which are predefined sequences of flow actions to execute repetitive tasks quickly, without requiring agent reasoning and orchestration at each step.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited billing page adds a reasoning-model premium of 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 billed tokens.
claims.quote: It's billed as Text and generative AI tools (premium) per 1000 tokens, at 10 Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Two indirect costs
claims.claim: Extra consumption from testing a refined copy is a real cost whatever the feature's final licence.
claims.quote: When you test an agent in the test chat, the agent's own activity, such as classic answers, generative answers, agent actions, and tenant graph grounding, doesn't consume Copilot Credits
claims.fix: Replace the unconditional testing-cost assertion with: 'Maker review, testing and publishing take time. Testing may also consume credits, depending on the harness and tools; this feature's harness and testing charges are not stated.' Cite this FAQ for standard-harness test-chat exemptions and the existing Microsoft Copilot harness cost page for billable testing. The cited Billing rates page also exempts agent-flow test runs.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: An agent's monthly Copilot Credit limit is set in Power Platform admin center under Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit.
claims.quote: 1. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. 2. Select Manage Agents. 3. Select the agent, and then select Set limit.
claims.fix: Retain the supported path, but qualify the guidance for resources still governed in Power Platform admin center. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-studio-costs and explain that Microsoft 365 resource-based policies take precedence for covered agents/environments; Manage capacity and Manage agent show which experience governs them.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The monthly-limit hard stop is optional through Stop usage.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Monthly agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop agent flows it calls, which are billed and capacity-checked separately.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately
